preconditions.description: The number of points n is between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a_i <= 10**9 and 1 <= b_i <= 10**9 and b_i != 0 for a_i, b_i, _, _ in points)
preconditions.description: For each point, the numerator and denominator of x_i (a_i, b_i) are integers between 1 and 10^9 inclusive, and b_i is non-zero.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= c_i <= 10**9 and 1 <= d_i <= 10**9 and d_i != 0 for _, _, c_i, d_i in points)
preconditions.description: For each point, the numerator and denominator of y_i (c_i, d_i) are integers between 1 and 10^9 inclusive, and d_i is non-zero.
The input contains exactly n points, where each point is represented as (a_i, b_i, c_i, d_i).

postconditions.description: The first line of output, c, is the number of moves performed.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= a <= n and 1 <= b <= n and a != b for a, b in moves)
postconditions.description: Each move consists of two distinct point indices between 1 and n inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(a not in used_points and b not in used_points for (a, b), used_points in zip(moves, [set(move) for move in moves[:-1]] + [set()]))
postconditions.description: No point is used in more than one move.

postconditions.expression: all(can_move(points, a, b) for a, b in moves)
postconditions.description: For each move (a, b), there exists a way to move points a and b such that the new coordinates of a, new coordinates of b, and (0, 0) are colinear.
The number of moves c is the maximum possible number of moves that can be performed under the given constraints.
